I will keep it simple and steady this year. I am 65, so I will not spread myself across too many crops. In Quzhou County, the wheat-maize rotation is what I know best, and it matches the land, the water conditions, and the way I can manage labor. I will keep the same land in winter wheat first, then follow with summer maize after harvest. That gives me food grain, cash income, and lower risk than trying something unfamiliar. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because they are more reliable for yield and lodging resistance. I will fertilize in a moderate way, not too heavily, because I want stable production and I do not want to waste money. I will irrigate when the crop really needs it, especially at the key stages, because water matters more than chasing every extra bit of yield. I will also keep pesticide sprays limited and only do what is needed for common diseases, insects, and weeds. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat ground preparation, and after wheat I will go into maize with no-tillage or very light disturbance so I can save time and catch soil moisture. My goal is not the highest possible yield. My goal is a crop plan I can manage well, with stable output and lower trouble.
